summary: Named after a pioneer, Baldy Hughes was a Pinetree Line radar station, closed in 1988; no readable source describes a fire lookout here.

evidence.supports: Distance of the station from Prince George (NBC Group figure, 19 miles)
evidence.quote: 19 miles southwest of the city of Prince George

evidence.supports: Distance of the station from Prince George (Wikipedia figure, 22.3 miles)
evidence.quote: It is located 22.3 miles (35.9 km) south-southwest of Prince George, British Columbia

evidence.supports: Station operated as part of the Pinetree Line
evidence.quote: It was operated as part of the Pinetree Line network controlled by NORAD

evidence.supports: Name taken from a pioneer called Hughes
evidence.quote: The radar station took its name after a rather colorful character, and early British Columbia pioneer, by the name of Hughes.

evidence.supports: Hughes known as Baldy; remount station on the Cariboo Wagon Road
evidence.quote: Hughes, who was often referred to by the name "Baldy", ran a remount station for the stage line that traveled the old Cariboo Wagon Road.

evidence.supports: Operations site on a nearby mountain bearing his name
evidence.quote: A nearby mountain, also bearing his name, was the location for the operations site.
Construction at the Baldy Hughes location had started during 1952.
Construction on the base began in 1952 and was completed in 1953.

evidence.supports: 918th AC&W Squadron arrived in 1955 (NBC Group account)
evidence.quote: In 1955, after construction was completed on the USAF's Baldy Hughes Air Station, the 918th AC&W Squadron moved in.
In June 1953, operations began at the unit's permanent home.

evidence.supports: Station handed to the RCAF on 1 March 1963
evidence.quote: the station was handed over to the RCAF on 1 March 1963

evidence.supports: Former station now houses the Baldy Hughes Addiction Treatment Centre
evidence.quote: Today the former station is The Baldy Hughes Addiction Treatment Centre.

sources.title: Baldy Hughes, BC: 1997 General History (The NBC Group)

notes_for_editor: The record is a fire lookout in the Canada Lookouts index, but none of the readable sources describes a lookout here. The Canada Lookouts page for Baldy Hughes (https://canada-lookouts.weebly.com/baldy-hughes.html) gives only the heading, Fraser - Fort George, and coordinates (53.617, -122.95). The story therefore covers the radar station on the same site. A BC Forest Fire Lookouts Facebook group post (https://www.facebook.com/groups/bcforestfirelookouts/posts/27708003845554853/) says a lookout was built in 1944, removed in 1951 when the US Air Force took the location for a radar station, and moved to the next mountain. Its text is not readable through fetch_text (only the page title is visible), so none of it is used; check it by hand before adding built or removed events. Sources disagree on the distance (19 miles vs 22.3 miles) and on the USAF move-in date (1955 per NBC Group; operations from June 1953 per Wikipedia), and both are stated in the story. The Wikipedia line about the treatment centre is a lead only; no second source was found. Access today is unknown. No events are recorded because none is a lookout event that a source supports.
